---
title: "Normalization, filters and blanks (3.8–3.12)"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("_prepare.R")
box::use(show = projlib/show, util = projlib/msdial_utils)
library(ggplot2)
raw <- tut$raw
tr <- tut$to_report
norm_se <- tr[["normalized"]]
best <- tr[["best normalization"]]
names_tbl <- SumExp::row_df(raw) |> tibble::rownames_to_column("feature_id") |> dplyr::select(feature_id, feature_name)
```

QuaNTA normalizes the peak areas with the internal standards in three ways and keeps all of them:

- **Closest RT**: each feature divided by the internal standard closest in retention time;
- **LOESS**: a smooth trend of the internal standards along the injection order, removed from
  every feature;
- **Multivariate (PCA)**: the main pattern shared by all internal standards, removed from every
  feature.

The method with the **lowest median RSD% among the QC replicates** is chosen as the default (here
`r tut$method_labels[[best]]`); you can choose another one on pages 4 and 5. After normalization, the
blanks are compared with the samples (blank filter) and subtracted.

```{r}
#| label: table-median-rsd
rsd <- tr[["median RSD% per normalization"]]
tut_table(tibble::tibble(Method = unname(tut$method_labels[names(rsd)]), `Median QC RSD%` = round(unname(rsd), 2),
                         Chosen = ifelse(names(rsd) == best, "✓", "")), height = "220px")
```

## 3.8 Comparison of normalization methods

```{r}
#| label: figure-3-8
#| fig-height: 5.5
# As the app with the batch "Global": after the blank filter and blank subtraction, without zeros
labs0 <- SumExp::name_labs(norm_se)
names(labs0) <- gsub(" .*", "", names(labs0))
prep <- show$qc_rsd_of_batch(tr[["qc rsd per group"]], "Global", labs0)
labs <- prep$labs
df <- prep$df |> dplyr::left_join(names_tbl, by = "feature_id")
rsd_txt <- apply(as.matrix(df[unname(labs)]), 1, function(v) {
  paste0(names(labs), ": ", ifelse(is.na(v), "no RSD%", paste0(round(v, 1), "%")), collapse = "<br>")
})
zero_txt <- ifelse(df$zeros == "", "", paste0("<br>Zeros left out: ", df$zeros, " of ", df$n))
df_long <- df |>
  dplyr::mutate(txt = paste0("<b>", feature_name, "</b> (", QC, ")<br>", rsd_txt, zero_txt,
                             "<br>Lowest: ", sub("^\\S+ ", "", as.character(sign)))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::all_of(unname(labs)), names_to = "Data", values_to = "RSD") |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(RSD)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Data = factor(Data, levels = unname(labs), labels = names(labs)))
p <- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = Data, y = RSD, group = feature_id, color = sign, text = txt)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5) + geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = show$norm_sign_colors, drop = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~QC) + labs(x = NULL, y = "RSD%", color = "Lowest RSD%")
plotly::ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") |>
  plotly::layout(legend = list(title = list(text = "Lowest RSD%<br>(click to filter)")))
```

Each line is one targeted compound in one QC group: its RSD% among the QC replicates without
normalization (Raw) and with each method, after the blank filter and blank subtraction. Zero values
(not detected, or at most the blank) are left out and counted in 3.9; a compound removed by the
blank filter, or with fewer than two values above 0, has no RSD%. The colour is the method that gave
that compound its lowest RSD%. Processed per batch, the label above the figure names the batch
chosen above table 3.1 (*Global*: all batches pooled; here *Global*).

**How to read it**

- **Lines going down** from Raw mean that normalization made the QC replicates more alike, as it
  should.
- **The colours** show which method works best for most compounds; the overall choice is the
  median in the table above.
- **Lines going up** are compounds that the internal standards do not represent well (e.g. a
  very different retention time or chemistry).

## 3.9 RSD% values

```{r}
#| label: table-3-9
t39 <- df |> dplyr::select(QC, Feature = feature_name, dplyr::all_of(unname(labs)), n, Zeros = zeros) |>
  dplyr::rename(dplyr::all_of(labs)) |> dplyr::mutate(QC = factor(QC))
tut_table(t39, search = TRUE) |> DT::formatRound(names(labs), 2)
```

The RSD% of 3.8 as a table: per compound, QC group and method. *n* is the number of QC injections
and *Zeros* the values left out (per method when they differ). Filter by QC group or search a
compound in the boxes above the columns.

## 3.10 Removed features

```{r}
#| label: table-3-10
rem <- tr[["removed features"]]
rem <- rem[rem$mat_id == best, ]
std <- SumExp::row_df(raw)$.std_type[match(rem$feature_id, rownames(raw))]
t310 <- tibble::tibble(
  Feature = rem$feature_name,
  Type = dplyr::case_when(rem$targeted ~ "Targeted", std %in% "vIS" ~ "Volumetric IS", TRUE ~ "Non-targeted"),
  `Removed by` = ifelse(rem$reason == "QC RSD%", "QC RSD%", paste0("Blank filter (≤ ", tr[["blank_filter_factor"]], "× blank)")),
  `QC RSD%` = round(rem$qc_rsd, 1)
) |> dplyr::arrange(Type != "Targeted", Feature)
tut_table(t310, height = "300px",
          caption = paste0(nrow(t310), " removed features (", sum(t310$Type == "Targeted"), " targeted, ",
                           sum(t310$Type == "Non-targeted"), " non-targeted)"))
```

The features removed for the chosen normalization method (here `r tut$method_labels[[best]]`) and
why:

- **Blank filter**: a feature is removed unless its maximum (or, with that option, mean) signal in
  the study samples (not the QCs or calibration standards) is more than `r tr[["blank_filter_factor"]]` × its average signal in the blanks; it is mostly
  contamination.
- **QC RSD% filter** (optional, off in this example): a feature is removed when its RSD% among the
  QC replicates is above the limit; it is measured too imprecisely. Processed per batch, its QC
  RSD% is the median over the batches (without the zero values).

In the app, the table has a search box and a filter above each column, e.g. to list only the
non-targeted features removed by the QC RSD% filter.

Removed targeted compounds are not calibrated; they appear at the end of table 4.1.

## 3.11 Blanks compared to samples

```{r}
#| label: figure-3-11
removed_blank <- rem$feature_id[rem$reason == "Blank filter" & rem$targeted]
tgt <- rownames(norm_se)[util$is_targeted_feature(norm_se)]
kept <- setdiff(tgt, rem$feature_id)
cd <- SumExp::col_df(norm_se)
keep <- cd$.ctrl_cat != "CalCurve"
smp <- tibble::as_tibble(cd[keep, ]) |> dplyr::mutate(group = show$sample_group(cd[keep, ]))
blank_plot <- function(fid, removed) {
  show$plotly_blank_comparison(
    y = unname(norm_se[[best]][fid, keep]), smp = smp, name = names_tbl$feature_name[match(fid, names_tbl$feature_id)],
    factor = tr[["blank_filter_factor"]], view = "groups", y_title = paste(tut$method_labels[[best]], "normalized"),
    subtitle = if (removed) "<span style='color:#c23636'><b>Removed by the blank filter</b></span>" else
      "<span style='color:#2E9E5B'><b>Kept by the blank filter</b></span>"
  )
}
if (length(removed_blank) > 0) blank_plot(removed_blank[1], TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: figure-3-11-kept
blank_plot(kept[1], FALSE)
```

One feature at a time: its normalized signal in the blanks (red) next to the QCs and the study
samples, before blank filtering and subtraction. The bars are the group means with their standard
deviation, the points the samples; the dashed line is the threshold of the blank filter
(`r tr[["blank_filter_factor"]]` × the blank mean). The first plot shows a compound the blank filter
removed, the second one it kept. In the app, choose *Per sample* for one bar per injection. After
a click in the figure (it gets a thin blue outline), the arrow keys ↑ / ↓ step through the features
and ← / → switch between *Groups* and *Per sample*; a click elsewhere on the page gives the keys back
to the internal standards (3.1, 3.5).

**How to read it**

- **Samples far above the threshold**: the compound is clearly measured; the blank level is
  subtracted.
- **Samples at the level of the blanks**: what is measured is mainly contamination from the
  procedure, and the feature is removed.
- **High blanks in one batch only** point to a contamination in that batch; blank subtraction is
  done per batch.

## 3.12 Features above the QC RSD% limit per batch

```{r}
#| label: figure-3-12
cnt <- tr[["qc rsd counts"]]
cnt <- cnt[cnt$mat_id == best, ]
show$plotly_qc_rsd_counts(cnt)
```

Per batch (and for all batches pooled), the number of targeted and non-targeted features whose QC
RSD% is above the limit, out of those with a QC RSD% (on each bar: above / all). The QC RSD% of a
feature is the median over the QC groups, after the blank filter and blank subtraction (processed
per batch: without the zero values). The limit is that of the QC RSD% filter; where the filter is
not used (as here), 30%, and the features are only counted, not removed. In the app, the figure
follows the normalization method chosen in 3.10.

**How to read it**

- **A batch with many more features above the limit** than the others had a problem (e.g. an
  unstable instrument, a bad QC preparation); look at its QCs in 3.5–3.7 and 4.6.
- **Many targeted compounds above the limit** in all batches suggest that the normalization does
  not suit them; compare the methods in 3.8.
